title: Drift fixture — NOT A REAL CONTRACT
description:
The negative control for generate-types.mjs. See drift-fixture-v1.contract.yaml. The committed TypeScript beside this file in generated/ is DELIBERATELY STALE and must stay that way: it is the known-failing input that proves the drift check can go red. Do not 'fix' it.

It exercises one of each node kind the renderer supports, so that a change to renderType which breaks a kind shows up here rather than in a real contract: a plain string, a bounded integer, an enum, a nullable via oneOf, an array with items, an object with required and optional properties, and a local $ref.

echoToken.description: An opaque token. Exercises the plain-string branch.

echoCount.description: Exercises the integer branch, which must render as `number` and not as a bounded type.

echoMode.description: Exercises the enum branch, which must render as a union of string literals.

echoLabelOrNull.description: Exercises the oneOf branch and the null type.

echoInput.description: Exercises required-versus-optional. `token` is required; `mode` and `count` are not.

echoOutput.description: Exercises the array branch and a nullable field.
